samples.text:
The table shows the average temperature, rainfall and sunshine hours for each month in a city called Port Sella.

Firstly, the temperature is lowest in January with 11°C and it goes up every month until July and August, when it reach 27°C. After that it goes down again to 20°C in October and 12°C in December.

Rainfall is very different. The wettest month is December with 110 mm, and January and November also have a lot of rain, 98 mm and 92 mm. From February the rain decrease, and in summer there is almost no rain, only 6 mm in June, 1 mm in July and 3 mm in August. Then it increases again in the autumn, for example 58 mm in October.

Sunshine is similar like the temperature. In December there is only 4.2 hours a day and in January 4.5 hours, but in July there is 11.8 hours, which is the most sunny month. June and August have 11.0 and 10.9 hours.

Overall, Port Sella has hot, dry and sunny summers and cool, wet winters with less sunshine.
samples.why: All three variables covered accurately · overview relevant but placed at the end · each variable described separately with simple linking · several verb-agreement and word-choice errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The table gives the average monthly temperature, rainfall and daily hours of sunshine in Port Sella over the course of a year.

Overall, the city has warm, dry and sunny summers, while its winters are cooler, wetter and much less sunny. Rainfall generally moves in the opposite direction to temperature and sunshine.

Temperatures are lowest in January, at 11°C, and rise steadily through spring to reach a peak of 27°C in July and August. They then fall again in autumn, dropping to 20°C in October and 12°C by December. Sunshine follows a very similar pattern, increasing from around four and a half hours a day in winter to a maximum of 11.8 hours in July, before declining to 4.2 hours in December, the least sunny month.

Rainfall, by contrast, is heaviest in the winter months. December is the wettest month, with 110 mm, followed by January (98 mm) and November (92 mm). From February onwards, the amount of rain falls considerably, and the summer is extremely dry, with only 6 mm in June, 1 mm in July and 3 mm in August. The rain then returns in autumn, rising to 58 mm in October.
samples.why: Clear overview of the seasonal pattern · temperature and sunshine logically combined · good cohesion and trend language · appropriate vocabulary · mostly accurate, though some approximation and slight repetition of month.

samples.text:
The table provides monthly averages for temperature, rainfall and daily sunshine in the city of Port Sella.

The data show a pronounced seasonal pattern, with hot, sunny and almost completely dry summers contrasting with mild, wet winters that receive considerably less sunshine. Temperature and sunshine rise and fall together, whereas rainfall follows the reverse pattern.

Temperatures climb gradually from a low of 11°C in January to a peak of 27°C in both July and August, a difference of 16 degrees, before falling back to 12°C in December. Hours of sunshine mirror this trend closely: the city receives only 4.5 hours a day in January and 4.2 in December, but almost three times as much in midsummer, when the figure reaches 11.8 hours in July.

Rainfall, in contrast, is concentrated in the cooler months. December is the wettest month, with 110 mm, and November and January are almost as wet, at 92 mm and 98 mm respectively. Precipitation then declines sharply through spring, to 22 mm in May, and virtually disappears in summer, with July recording just 1 mm. The rains return from September, when 18 mm falls, rising steeply to 58 mm in October.
samples.why: Well-placed overview explaining how the variables relate · figures selected purposefully with accurate derived comparisons · cohesion effortless · precise vocabulary (mirror, precipitation) · wide range of structures, error-free.
